title: Fruits & vegetables
blurb: Asian and tropical fruit, Chinese greens and the Western vegetables on restaurant menus.

groups.name: Asian & tropical fruits
groups.intro: The fruits on Hong Kong market stalls and in gift boxes.

items.name: Durian
items.what: Spiky 'king of fruits' with custard-like flesh and a famously strong smell; Musang King is the prized variety.

items.name: Mangosteen
items.what: Deep purple shell hiding sweet-sour white segments; the 'queen of fruits'.

items.name: Lychee
items.what: Bumpy red shell and juicy, translucent white flesh; at its best in June.

items.name: Longan
items.what: 'Dragon eye': small tan-shelled fruit, like a milder lychee.

items.name: Rambutan
items.what: Hairy red cousin of the lychee.

items.name: Dragon fruit
items.what: Pink scaly skin with white or magenta flesh and tiny black seeds.

items.name: Jackfruit
items.what: The biggest tree fruit: sweet yellow pods inside; young ones are cooked as a meat substitute.

items.name: Pomelo
items.what: Giant thick-skinned citrus, a Mid-Autumn and New Year favourite.

items.name: Persimmon
items.what: Orange autumn fruit, crisp or jelly-soft when ripe; also dried.

items.name: Starfruit
items.what: Star-shaped when sliced; juicy and tart.

items.name: Yuzu
items.what: Knobbly Japanese citrus prized for its fragrant zest in desserts and cocktails.

items.name: Shine Muscat grapes
items.what: Large, very sweet green Japanese grapes with edible skin, sold as luxury gifts.

groups.name: Asian vegetables
groups.intro: The greens and roots in Cantonese cooking, and their English names.

items.name: Bok choy
items.what: Mild cabbage with thick white stalks and dark green leaves.

items.name: Choy sum
items.what: Tender greens with small yellow flowers, the standard blanched vegetable at cha chaan tengs.

items.name: Gai lan
items.what: Chinese broccoli: thick stems and broad leaves, served with oyster sauce at yum cha.

items.name: Water spinach
items.what: Hollow-stemmed greens stir-fried with garlic or fermented bean curd (also kangkung, ong choy).

items.name: Daikon
items.what: Long white radish, used in turnip cake and Japanese simmered dishes.

items.name: Bitter melon
items.what: Bumpy green gourd with a famously bitter taste.

items.name: Winter melon
items.what: Huge pale-green melon used in clear soups.

items.name: Shiitake
items.what: Dark, meaty mushroom, often dried for deeper flavour.

items.name: Enoki
items.what: Clusters of thin white mushrooms, a hot-pot staple.

items.name: Taro
items.what: Starchy root with purple-flecked flesh, used in desserts and dim sum.

groups.name: Western vegetables & herbs
groups.intro: Names that confuse people on menus, including UK versus US words.

items.name: Artichoke
items.what: Thistle bud: you eat the soft base of each leaf and the heart.

items.name: Asparagus
items.what: Green or white spears; white asparagus season (Spargelzeit) is a big deal in Germany.

items.name: Aubergine / eggplant
items.what: Glossy purple vegetable: aubergine in the UK, eggplant in the US.

items.name: Courgette / zucchini
items.what: Green summer squash: courgette in the UK, zucchini in the US.

items.name: Fennel
items.what: Crunchy white bulb with feathery fronds and an aniseed taste.

items.name: Kale
items.what: Curly dark-green cabbage, the 2010s superfood.

items.name: Rocket / arugula
items.what: Peppery salad leaf: rocket in the UK, arugula in the US.

items.name: Truffle
items.what: Prized underground fungus shaved over pasta: white from Alba, black from Périgord.

items.name: Avocado
items.what: Creamy green fruit used like a vegetable, from guacamole to toast.

items.name: Coriander / cilantro
items.what: The herb people love or hate: coriander in the UK, cilantro in the US.
